verse: Male and female he created them. And God blessed them, saying: Increase and multiply. (Gen 1:27-28)
The Lord God said: “It is not good for man to be alone: I will make him a helper as his partner.” (Gen 2:18)

For the man there was not found a helper like himself. Then the Lord God cast a deep sleep upon him: and when he was fast asleep, he took one of his ribs and closed up the flesh in its place. And the rib which the Lord God had taken from the man, He made into a woman and brought her to the man. (Gen 2:20-22)

The man said, “This now is bone of my bones, and flesh of my flesh; she shall be called woman, because she was taken out of man.” Therefore, a man shall leave his father and mother and shall cling to his wife: and they shall become one flesh. (Gen 2:23-24)
He created them, male and female; and he blessed them. (Gen 5:2)

“Have you not read that he who made man from the beginning, made them male and female?” And he said: “For this reason, a man shall leave his father and mother, and he shall cling to his wife, and these two shall become one flesh.” (Matt 19:4-5)
They are not two, but one flesh. What therefore God has joined together, let no man separate. (Matt 19:6)
You should consider all the works of the Most High: they come in pairs, one opposite the other. (Sir 33:15)
A man shall leave behind his father and mother, and he shall cling to his wife; and the two shall be as one flesh. This is a great mystery. (Eph 5:31-32)
Let marriage be held in honor by all, and let the marriage bed be kept undefiled, for God will judge the sexually immoral and adulterers. (Heb 13:4)

Issac led her into the tent of Sarah his mother, and he took Rebekah and she became his wife. And he loved her so much, that it moderated the sorrow which befell him at his mother’s death. (Gen 24:67)

It is better for two to be together, than for one to be alone. For they have the advantage of their companionship. If one falls, he shall be supported by the other. Woe to one who is alone. For when he falls, he has no one to lift him up. (Eccl 4:9-10)
If two lie together, they can keep each other warm. How can one be warm alone? (Eccl 4:11)
Be subject to one another in the fear of Christ. (Eph 5:21)
Live joyfully with the wife whom you love, all the days of your fleeting life which have been given to you under the sun. (Eccl 9:9)

My spirit is pleased with three things; these are approved in the sight of God and mortals: the harmony of brothers, and the love of neighbors, and a husband and wife agreeing well together. (Sir 25:1)

Yet truly, in the Lord man is not independent of woman, nor woman independent of man. For just as woman came into existence from man, so also does man came to existence through woman. But all things are from God. (1 Cor 11:11-12)
The unbelieving husband has been sanctified through the believing wife, and the unbelieving wife has been sanctified through the believing husband. (1 Cor 7:14)

Happy is the husband of a good wife. For the number of his years is doubled. A good wife delights her husband, and she will fill up the years of his life with peace. A good wife is a good portion, given to the man who fears the Lord. (Sir 26:1-3)

I will take you to be my wife forever; I will take you to be my wife in righteousness, justice, steadfast love, and in compassion. I will betroth you to me in faithfulness; and you shall know the Lord. (Hos 2:19)

Husbands, love your wives, just as Christ also loved the Church and handed himself over for her, so that he might sanctify and cleanse her with the washing of water by the Word, so that he might offer her to himself as a glorious Church, not having any spot or wrinkle or any such thing, so that she would be holy and without blemish. (Eph 5:25-27)

A husband should fulfill his conjugal obligation to his wife, and a wife should also act similarly toward her husband. It is not the wife, but the husband, who has authority over her body. But, similarly also, it is not the husband, but the wife, who has authority over his body. (1 Cor 7:3-4)
I want you to know that the head of every man is Christ, and the head of the woman is the man. And the head of Christ is God. (1 Cor 11:3)
The husband is the head of the wife, just as Christ is the head of the Church. (Eph 5:23)
Husbands, live with your wives in an understanding way, bestowing honor on the wife as the weaker vessel and as co-heirs of the life of grace, so that your prayers may not be hindered. (1 Pet 3:7)
Husbands, love your wives, and do not be bitter against them. (Col 3:19)

Husbands should love their wives as their own bodies. He who loves his wife loves himself. For no man has ever hated his own flesh, but instead he nourishes and cherishes it, as Christ also does to the Church. (Eph 5:28-29)
Yet truly, each and every one of you should love his wife as himself. and the wife is to respect her husband. (Eph 5:33)

Blessed is everyone who fears the Lord, who walks in his ways. You shall eat the labor of your hands; you shall be happy, and it shall be well with you. Your wife will be like a fruitful vine in your house; (Ps 128:1-3)
He who gets to a good wife establishes a possession. She is a helper in agreement with him, and she is a pillar of rest. (Sir 36:29)
A house and its riches are inherited from parents. But a prudent wife is from the Lord. (Pro 19:14)
He who has found a good wife has found goodness, and he shall obtain favor from the Lord. (Pro 18:22)
Do not choose to depart from a wise and good wife, whom you have been allotted in the fear of the Lord. For the grace of her modesty is above gold. (Sir 7:26)

Wives, be subject to your husbands, so that, even if some do not believe the word, they may be won over without a word, through the conduct of their wives, when they see your reverent and chaste behavior. (1 Pet 3:1-2)
Everyone who divorces his wife and marries another commits adultery. And whoever marries her who has been divorced by her husband commits adultery. (Luk 16:18)

Preserve your spirit, and do not despise the wife of your youth. For I hate divorce, says the Lord, the God of Israel, and covering one’s garment with violence, says the Lord of hosts. Preserve your spirit, and do not be willing to be faithless. (Mal 2:15-16)
Wives, submit yourselves to your husbands, as is fitting in the Lord. (Col 3:18)

Wives submit yourselves to your husband, as to the Lord. For the husband is the head of the wife, just as Christ is the head of the Church, and he is the Savior of his body. Therefore, just as the Church is subject to Christ, so also should wives be subject to their husbands in all things. (Eph 5:22-24)
To them that are married, not I but the Lord commands, that the wife should not separate from her husband, and that the husband should not divorce his wife. (1 Cor 7:10-11)

A grace of a diligent woman delights her husband, and her skill puts flesh on his bones. Such is a wise and silent woman is a gift from the Lord, and there is nothing is more precious than a well instructed soul. (Sir 26:13-14)
Bear one another’s burdens, and so you will fulfill the law of Christ. (Gal 6:2)
Love one another with brotherly affection; surpass one another in showing honor. (Rom 12:10-11)

I give you a new commandment: Love one another. Just as I have loved you, so also must you love one another. By this, all shall recognize that you are my disciples: if you will have love for one another. (Jn 13:34-35)

Love is patient and kind; it is not envious, does not deal perversely, and is not puffed up; love is not rude or self-seeking or irritable; love does not keep a record of wrongs; love does not rejoice in iniquity, but rejoices in the truth. Love bears all things; believes all things, hopes all things, and endures all things. (1 Cor 13:4-7)
Above all these things, put on love, which ties everything together in perfect unity. (Col 3:14)
Amen I say to you, whatever you do for one of the least of these brothers and sisters of mine, you do it for me. (Matt 25:40)
In all things, do to others what you want them to do to you. (Matt 7:12)
Beloved, let us love one another, for love is from God, and everyone who loves is born of God and knows God. The one who does not love does not know God, for God is love. (1 Jn 4:7-8)
You should owe nothing to anyone, but to love one another. For whoever loves his neighbor has fulfilled the law. (Rom 13:8)
Let us not only love in word or speech, but in action and in truth. (1 Jn 3:18)
